newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar likely to fall in Asia on Japan's c/a data.
newsitem.headline: Dollar likely to fall in Asia on Japan's c/a data.

text.p: The dollar is likely to fall against the yen on Wednesday in Asia as Japan's current account surplus for April is seen showing a sharp increase from a year earlier, dealers said.

The data, to be released at 2350 GMT (Tuesday), may knock the dollar down below Tuesday's New York low of around 111.60 yen and stop-loss sales at 111.50 yen may take it down further to 111.00 yen, said a trust bank dealer.
"The market is closely focusing on the release of Japan's current account data, shifting away from interest rate factors," he added.

A Reuters poll of economists showed, on average, that April current account surplus would grow to 1.13 trillion yen, compared with a surplus of 566.6 billion yen last year. The forecasts ranged from 990 billion yen to 1.21 trillion yen.
The trust bank dealer said a sharp increase in the surplus could trigger a wave of dollar sales, with stop-loss sales related to "knock-out" positions seen at 111.50 yen.

"The market is eager to see the dollar's break of 110 yen," said the trust bank dealer. But possible supportive remarks by Japanese government officials could prevent the dollar from falling below 111.00 yen for today in Asia, he added.
The bank dealer said U.S. funds are likely to buy back the dollar at around 111.00 yen.
But a city bank dealer said major buyers have stayed away from the market and the Japanese are becoming extremely bearish about the prospects for the dollar.
She said follow-through selling by Japanese exporters may drag the dollar down.

The topside will be limited at around 112.50 yen even if the April current account surplus is smaller than expected. Japanese exporters and investors could move to sell dollars actively if the dollar should rebound to 113 yen, dealers said.
The dollar is likely to stay relatively solid against the mark, with worries about a delay in the start of a single European currency receding.

French President Jacques Chirac reaffirmed on Tuesday the government's commitment to a punctual launch of the euro. He also said he hoped the European Union stability pact -- an agreement that sets out budgetary criteria for participants in monetary union -- would be agreed to at a summit in Amsterdam next Monday and Tuesday.
The mark is likely to fall against the yen, with a dip below 65.00 yen seen possible, dealers said.
